newsitem.title: JAPAN: Typhoon Violet moves towards central Japan.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Violet moves towards central Japan.

text.p: Typhoon Violet, packing maximum winds of 126 kph (79 mph), was moving closer to central Japan on Sunday, forcing the cancellation of dozens of domestic flights, the Meteorological Agency said.
As of 9.00 a.m. (0000 GMT) on Sunday, Violet was located 510 km (319 miles) southwest of Tokyo, the agency said.
Violet, the 17th typhoon to hit Japan this year, was moving northeast at a speed of 35 kph (22 mph), it said.
Because of the typhoon, at least 23 domestic flights and several ferry services were cancelled, authorities said.
There were no reports of damage or casualties.

The typhoon was likely to start striking the southern part of Izu Peninsula, a popular hot-spring resort, at around noon (0300 GMT) on Sunday, before hitting areas along the Pacific coast near Tokyo, the agency said.
The agency predicted that the typhoon would dump up to 30 cm (12 inches) of rain.
